judgments.evidence: src/build.jl:576-580 and 616-619: Outputs holds `components::Vector{ComponentOutputs}` (each `path`, `stage1`, `stage2`, which are port-name vectors) and `order::Vector{Int}`. It holds no stage names. Probe P3: `ComponentOutputs("c", [:out], Symbol[])`.
judgments.fix: On [`Outputs`](#g-outputs) (the nominal evaluation's product, the port classes and the execution order) it is plain printable data ([§9.2][s9-2]), namely paths, the port names each stage produces, and order.
judgments.note: The phrase "paths, stage names, order" comes from f9e2cacb's old §14.7, which described the Build's schedule. D-253 and the glossary entry g-outputs (spec.md:16775) now describe per-component stage-1/stage-2 port name sets. Paths and order match. "Stage names" is wrong only if read literally, since D-253 itself says "stage-1 and stage-2 name sets".

judgments.evidence: src/store.jl:11-13 `struct CellAddr{P,K}; offsets::NTuple{K,Int}` has one offset per distinct leaf eltype. src/build.jl:433-434 builds it with `length(eltypes)` offsets. Probe P2: MixedCell's port address is `CellAddr{TaggedValue{Float64},2}` with offsets (0, 0), across the Float64 and Int blocks. test/test_store.jl:56-61 does the same. Field carriage and the port-type parameter match: executor.jl:56-60, store.jl:11.
judgments.fix: A cell address is a build-time offset into each block its leaves occupy, one per element type, so a mixed-leaf cell spans several blocks. The offsets are carried in an entry *field*, with the port type as the address's own parameter.
judgments.note: The spec never says that a cell can span several element-type blocks. The store.jl:1-9 comment cites a 2026-08-20 'C2M' bench that appears in no spec or log text. D-162's Position says 'build-time offsets' in the plural, which fits either reading.

judgments.evidence: src/build.jl:1530-1551 sends continuous updates to rhs_entries (RHSEntry) and discrete ones to tick_entries (UpdateEntry). Lines 1611-1614 bind them as `rhs` and `ticks`. src/executor.jl:172-188: an RHSEntry writes only its own x_off slice of ẋbuf, and an UpdateEntry writes only its own sstore ('written by this entry, and by nothing else', executor.jl:93). Both read the table and never another entry's product.

Every loop call site calls rhs with no index: src/model.jl:619 and 632, src/trim.jl:602 and 744. rhs has no gated entries (build.jl:1545 pushes `nothing` gates), so its two chunk tuples share one type (probe P4: 'same tuple types: true').
judgments.note: `rhs(tick)` is still a legal call. PhaseBody{I,I}(tick) (executor.jl:578) ignores the index and walks the interior, and test_executor.jl:21 and 141-143 pin that, so the roster is total in both arities. No index ever reaches rhs semantically. If the sentence is read as 'rhs accepts no argument', the code is broader than the spec.
